title: What is model() — two-way signal binding with model inputs?
description: Explain model() for replacing @Input + @Output pairs.
answer:
**TL;DR:** model() is a writable signal input combining input + output — parent uses [(prop)] banana-in-box.
`value = model(0)` declares a writable signal input that also acts as output. Parent binds with banana-in-box `[(value)]="parentSig"` (or `[(value)]` with `model.required`). Inside child, `value()` reads and `value.set()`/`update()` writes — automatically emits `valueChange` event for parent. This replaces ` @Input value + @Output valueChange = new EventEmitter` for two-way binding. `model` respects `alias` and is signal-reactive (`computed(()=>value()*2)`). Unlike `input()`, `model()` is writable — use for controls that parent and child co-own. Introduced in Angular 17.2 as replacement for `input`+`output` two-way pattern. | Pattern | Declare | Parent syntax | |---|---|---| | Separate | `@Input v + @Output vChange` | `[v] + (vChange)` | | `model()` | `v = model(0)` | `[(v)]` | **Interview Tip:** Say: 'For two-way binding I use model() — the child calls value.update() and the parent banana-in-box stays in sync without manual emit.' ```ts import { Component, model } from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector:'app-counter', standalone:true, template:` `}) export class CounterComponent { count = model(0); // two-way signal } // Parent // ```
